reviews.title: Already stellar app, just got WAY BETTER
reviews.text:
AuDHD programmer, artist, and passionate nerd here! Get ready, this is a long one. 

It’s like the Goblin Tools team knew I needed the Taskmaster and made it so I could use it today. Just checked my Magic To Do and I got 14 things done today!! I used voice to text in the Compiler to say what I needed to do, sent the list to the Magic To-Do, and used TaskMaster to get it done!! 

Turns out I didn’t even need the tasks broken down, I just needed that organized method to focus on one thing at a time. If I wanted to add something else, I just put it on the list instead of feeling like I needed to stay sidetracked. 

Only suggestion I have is this: please integrate a way to continue the Taskmaster stopwatch when phone is asleep or when app is inactive. I would love to track how long it actually takes me to do these tasks, but when I put my phone on sleep, I opened it after completing some tasks and it said it took me 13 seconds… 

An added bonus would be to allow us to fully hide the next tasks. Maybe a toggle to customize the display? That way we can either do the default with 3 tasks showing OR we can blur the following two tasks so they only show when we scroll. That or really just focus on the one thing at a time and only show the list when we choose to see it. 

Incredible work, Goblin Tools team! I’ll be sure to make a monthly donation once I get more steady income.

reviews.title: Great app, I have a suggestion!
reviews.text:
Goblin Tools is an amazing app, and I have been using it for a few years now. Whenever I get stuck, I sometimes remember that I have Goblin Tools, and it has helped me prioritize my tasks and get things done.

I do have one suggestion. Magic ToDo is one of my favorite tools, and I love how it can break things into smaller tasks. However, I wish I could give the AI more information about what a task involves without giving it a long title.

For example, let's say I have a task that says something like "work on anthropology essay." It breaks the task down into the general steps I would need to complete, but if there are specific things I have to do for the essay, the AI wouldn't know that from just the title. I wish we could describe what the task involves or what the general routine for completing it looks like so that the AI knows how to break it into steps without being too vague. Essentially, it would be like the Compiler, but for one individual ToDo list item.

Goblin Tools is an awesome app, and it was worth spending the three dollars on it instead of using the website. 10 out of 10, would recommend. ✨

reviews.title: Great premise, botched execution
reviews.text:
I never leave reviews, but I am genuinely disappointed in this app. The lack of support on the app’s main website or other place to voice feedback has brought me here. I truly do think it is a great and could be an indispensable tool for neurodivergent people, or really anyone, in assisting executive function. It truly made my life so much easier to categorize and process. It acted as a secondary, working brain that genuinely helped me get through some extremely rough patches.

However, frequent crashes, buggy features, and lagging synchronization between devices affecting already finished lists have made me hate using it. The latest feature, adding tabs in the MagicToDo list, was a brilliant addition that I thought would be amazing. I loaded a lot of things from my main to do list onto that new tabs, hoping to better manage my many categories of things to remember. 

…Then they disappeared. I didn’t even see when it happened. The whole tab wiped clean. And I tried using the built-in back button, refreshing my page, nothing. All of it gone. I wrote down what I could remember on a separate piece of paper, and thankfully, I have some of the tasks backed up in other places, but now most of the ones I only had in Goblin Tools are just gone with no way to get them back. 

In a panic, I opened the app on my phone, hoping to catch the things I missed since I can always count on it to lag during sync...it was halfway into syncing and didn’t catch anything new that I had written NOR had it kept the old stuff. But the WEBSITE synced immediately and erased ALL of it. I was able to back out on the website and get the previously wrecked list back, but it’s still wrecked. 

So that’s it for me. I will be uninstalling the app and finding a different task management solution. Use this app at your own caution. I was really excited to support this project since it’s been so beneficial in my life. But that’s what it is. A project. The lack of customer support options makes that clear. I should have paid more attention. You are a test subject benefiting from an ongoing AI project. It’s great for small tasks and light projects, but be very wary and back everything up somewhere else. Do not use it for large, time spanning tasks or projects. Especially if you don’t have great working memory.

Not sure what a text message means for your relationship, get some clues from the judge that reads emotional context and nuance and gives really insightful analysis of the exchange! Can’t get your email or text to sound less intense or to say what you mean in a more tactful or more precessional way, use the formalizer! Need your to do list broken down into smaller tasks, or need to know how long to plan to do a task, use the magic to do, the estimator, or the compiler! Need to be able to make decision and can’t figure out how, use the consultant! It creates a pros cons list and then gives advice based on that list and it is scarily helpful. Need to learn about something quickly and know what you need to know without getting lost down an internet rabbit hole, use the professor! The professor will even give an example to help move the knowledge from interesting information to application. All this and more … and you can set the spicy level to let it know how much help you need. 

There appear to be copycats for this app! We This is the real one! Also, they have it for free on the website https://goblin.tools, but I find the app really convenient. The interface is basic which  makes it easier to focus on the content and not get lost on the screen.

reviews.title: Even better than description
reviews.text:
The magic to-do list breaks your tasks into sub-tasks, yeah, and it does that wonderfully, but guess what? it also adds a button to do that to each sub-task, and then to each sub-sub-task, and that goes on and on. You can click the pepper emoji button to make sure it'll break tasks down into a higher or lower number of subtasks, and ask for an estimate of time for each task or sub-task (as far as I've seen, it's been pretty accurate). And that's only the to-do list part of the app! The Professor is really great at explaining things, the Consultant can help even with specific things like little-known companies and services, it has internet access so you don't have to limit yourself to what you think it'd know about. The Judge seemed pretty good when I tested it but I don't have trouble with that so I never use it and don't have an opinion on it. I haven't tried using the Chef or Compiler yet, but they sound pretty cool!

If there's one thing I wish would change, it'd be to have the app's theme change according to the system theme. I actually spent days using the app without realizing there was a dark mode button, it was funny.

reviews.title: Thank Goodness! Finally!
reviews.text:
I am at the higher end of the scale for ADHD with extreme anxiety and overwhelming procrastination that affects every part of my life anymore.  I always know exactly what needs to be done. I know that I have to do things, but I become overwhelmed because I only see big picture of all of those items and it’s the details that I stress over thinking about so therefore I just don’t do any of it because I either want it all done right away, I just won’t do it. I put in the first most stressful of tasks that I must do and that I put off for almost a year and asked the App to expand the details of what that meant and what I might need to do and it included everything, including just the surroundings of a peaceful environment in which for me to begin that task with that most no one, or any other App has ever considered, calms my mind and calms my presence to be able to even begin thinking of those details and then to begin working on them. This life-saving app immediately broke down this to do and one of the very first items it  considered was my environment being set up first knowing that would help my calmness and being able to achieve this task without interruption and actually accounted for those types of interruptions that I might encounter which undoubtedly leads me to avoiding the entire thing. It also gave me an estimate of how long it may take for preparation and for completing the very helpful and detailed tasks. Immediately after seeing the thorough and thoughtfulness of the details to consider and the estimated time to complete everything allowed me to breathe deeply and took away that overwhelming anxiety almost immediately and completely. 
 I can now look at that item, (which has eaten away at my well being over the last year), broken down into logical reasonable workable details without feeling like something is missing, removing the guilt and anxiousness I’ve suffered from and just redshifted my brain towards actually wanting to work through each item until it’s finally completed and out of my head and body! Overly dramatic or exaggerated as that may sound or as some form of excuse, it’s taken years of working with my ADHD coach to understand the ‘why’ of what or how I do what I do to then ultimately help formulate my day to day routines into workable solutions based on my ADHD world view. Thank you so very much!

reviews.title: Cute and Clever
reviews.text:
This app is wonderful, I used goblin tools on PC for a while and it’s great. Though I’ve been using it a while, I hadn’t actually been formally diagnosed until July 2024 as an adult. So I hope no one feels gatekept by it, but rather it can affirm that even if they’re not clinically ADHD, they do have many of the symptoms and can utilize it for both productivity… and play!

It is very fun to have it infinitely break down the simplest steps until it’s egregious. My (also neurodivergent, I think) brother and I once sat and had it continue to break down the first step on the highest level and we were giggling the entire time. It’s a good tool, and the AI works very well: even on a task like opening your eyes!

It tickled us when one of the steps was “realize that your eyes are closed.” 😂😂

The slightly philosophical takeaway is that those of us with such executive function limitations often live in perpetual anxiety over feeling as if we desperately need to do [something] while simultaneously being paralyzed and unable to do it. This tool can help with both. 

Knowing you have a tool that was developed and still offered for free (on PC), from a creator who saw a need, even within their own life, as opposed to a trendy “ADHD Helper!” utility whose purpose was crafted in a boardroom. If those kinds of apps help, they’re great and should continue to exist and grow!

But, if you find them all useful and want to pick something to stick with, I recommend goblin.tools for the reasons mentioned. Spoonies are encouraged by the virtual tribe we have cultivated online, and there is comfort in knowing we are working together, either by creating something or using, supporting, and promoting it!

And again, this IS NOT just for neurodivergents. Anyone can and should benefit from the tool!

Overall, 10/5 stars. Would recommend. 🤗

reviews.title: Send My Compliments to “The Chef”
reviews.text:
I personally find Magic ToDo to be the most useful tool because I really struggle with breaking things down into manageable parts. It’s not always 100% accurate, but it gives me a much better starting place.  

You might want to tweak “The Chef” a little bit. I have a rather empty fridge at the moment and I think eating a “Monster Energy Pizza Casserole” would probably kill me. 

I entered my ingredients as follows: 

one can of monster energy, leftover pizza, condiments, four ears of corn, rice, oatmeal, pinto beans, canned diced tomatoes, spoiled kale, protein powder 

The recipe:

Monster Energy Pizza Casserole

Serving Size: 4

Ingredients:

- 1 can of Monster Energy (473 ml / 16 fl oz)

- 2 slices of leftover pizza

- 4 ears of corn

- Rice (200 g / 7 oz)

- Canned diced tomatoes (400 g / 14 oz)

- Protein powder (30 g / 1 oz)

Instructions:

1. Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).

2. In a large mixing bowl, tear the leftover pizza slices into small pieces.

3. Cut the corn kernels off the ears of corn and add them to the bowl.

4. Add cooked rice, canned diced tomatoes, and protein powder to the bowl. Mix well to combine all ingredients.

5. Pour the can of Monster Energy over the mixture and stir until everything is evenly coated.

6. Transfer the mixture to a baking dish and spread it out evenly.

7. Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, until the casserole is heated through and slightly crispy on top.

8. Serve hot and enjoy your Monster Energy Pizza Casserole!

I also love the other features of the app. It can estimate how long a task will take (amazing for planning), tell you how to change the tone of a message to make it more/less professional, and tell you what the tone of messages is. 

This is the only app I’ve ever paid for, and it’s absolutely worth it. It’s only 99 cents one time, and it has no ads. I’ve absolutely used it more than enough to make up for the 99 cents I spent.
